title: Fund your team uniforms with sponsors & fundraising
meta_title: Fund Team Uniforms: Sponsors & Fundraising | MOMUTO
meta_descript: Fund your soccer uniforms with local sponsors, booster clubs and registration fees: printed sponsor logos at no extra cost and quantity discounts.
summary: How club and rec teams pay for uniforms: local business sponsors with logos printed in at no extra cost, what a sponsor gets, and booster-club fundraising or registration fees when there's no sponsor.
content:
Quick answer

Most teams don’t pay for uniforms out of pocket — they fund them with a local sponsor, the booster club, or registration fees. Sublimation prints a sponsor’s logo into the fabric at no extra cost, and one local business sponsor often covers a large part of a roster order. No minimum order.

Sponsors: the usual way to pay for uniforms

A local restaurant, auto shop, realtor or family-owned business will often sponsor a club or rec team in exchange for their logo on the jersey. Sublimation prints that logo on the chest, sleeves or back — permanently, with no extra cost per logo. Design it free in the 3D designer, or send a concept to a designer for a $15 deposit, credited in full to orders of 5+ jerseys — free for a team order.

What a sponsor gets

Every practice, every game-day photo, every team roster page carries the logo. It is cheap, local advertising with goodwill attached — which is exactly why so many small businesses say yes. Offer the chest for the main sponsor, sleeves and back for smaller ones.

Booster clubs, registration fees, and fundraising when there’s no sponsor

No sponsor yet? Most club teams and school programs already have a structure built for exactly this. A booster club can budget uniforms into its annual fundraising, alongside concessions and spirit-wear sales. Many rec leagues fold a uniform allotment straight into the registration fee, so families pay once at sign-up instead of chasing a separate collection. Where neither applies, split the cost across the roster — there’s no minimum order, so each player can pay for their own jersey — or sell a few extra jerseys to family and supporters. The per-jersey price drops with quantity, so a bigger order is cheaper per jersey.

Frequently asked questions

How much does a sponsor logo cost to add?

Nothing extra. Sublimation prints every logo into the fabric at no additional cost, whether you have one sponsor or several.

Where can sponsor logos go?

Chest, sleeves and back. A common setup is a main sponsor on the chest and smaller ones on the sleeves or back.

Can a booster club or registration fee cover uniforms?

Yes. Many booster clubs budget team uniforms into their annual fundraising, and many rec leagues build a uniform allotment into the registration fee families already pay at sign-up.

Can each player pay for their own jersey?

Yes — there is no minimum order, so you can split the order across the roster and still get the quantity discount.
